item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis from 26 to 28. There are four marks in between 26 to 27, as well as in between 27 to 28. K is marked underneath the last mark between 27 and 28.]

Which number does K represent on this number line?
item.figure_description: A horizontal number line with arrowheads at both ends. There are evenly spaced vertical tick marks. The first labeled tick mark is labeled 26 below the line. Between 26 and 27, there are 4 evenly spaced tick marks dividing the interval into 5 equal parts. The tick mark for 27 is labeled below the line. Between 27 and 28, there are 4 evenly spaced tick marks, with the fourth tick mark labeled with the letter K below the line. The next tick mark is labeled 28 below the line. The line extends slightly past 26 to the left and past 28 to the right.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis, from 0 to 2. Two dots are shown, “P” and “Q”. “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1 and “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1.]

P and Q represent two fractions on the number line above.

P × Q = N.

Which of these shows the location of N on the number line?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lays roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies halfway between 1 and 2.]

reference_items.figure_description:
The figure above the text shows a horizontal number line with an arrow at the right end. There are tick marks labeled 0, 1, and 2, with equal spacing between 0 and 1 and between 1 and 2. Between 0 and 1, two points are marked with black dots: point P is labeled below the line at approximately 0.5 (halfway between 0 and 1), and point Q is labeled below the line at approximately 0.75 (three-fourths of the distance from 0 to 1).

Each of the four response options shows the same number line with points P and Q in their original positions, along with a third point labeled N above the line:
- Option A: Point N is marked halfway between 1 and 2, at approximately 1.5.
- Option B: Point N is marked between Q and 1, at approximately 0.85.
- Option C: Point N is marked between P and Q, at approximately 0.625.
- Option D: Point N is marked between 0 and P, at approximately 0.25.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The diagram shows a system for locating points

[Image: A group of 6 concentric circles with origin “O”. Degrees from 0 to 360 are marked in 10 degree intervals where 0 and 360 are marked on a line “A” that goes across all circles. The 6 concentric circles are labeled from 1 to 6 along line “A”.]

In this system, the position of a point P is described by its distance from origin, O, and the amount of counterclockwise turn from a baseline OA to OP. Thus, the coordinates of P are (5, 340°).

A. Mark the points B (3, 30°) and C (4, 120°) on the graph above.
B. Draw the angle BOC. What is the measure of angle BOC?

Angle BOC = ____°

descriptors: Both points correctly marked (pictured on right) [Image: A line drawn from O to B where B is the point where the third circle intersects the 30 degree mark. Figure also has a line drawn from O to C where C is the point where the fourth circle intersects the 120 degree mark.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Correct value given for incorrect point(s) drawn in A
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: Two score points will be given if both parts A and B are correct. One score point will be given if only part A is correct. No credit is given if only part B is correct.
reference_items.figure_description: A circular polar coordinate grid centered at an origin O, formed by 6 concentric circles. A horizontal baseline ray extends right from O, labeled A at its end, with the 6 concentric circles labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 along this ray. Radial line segments extend from O every 10° around the full circle, labeled on the outer rim counterclockwise from 0° at ray OA through 10°, 20°, 30°, up to 350°. A point labeled P is plotted on the 5th circle along the 340° radial line.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Three brothers, Bob, Dan, and Mark, receive a gift of 45,000 zeds from their father. The money is shared between the brothers in proportion to the number of children each one has. Bob has 2 children, Dan has 3 children, and Mark has 4 children.

How many zeds does Mark get?

[Image: A ruler measuring the length of a pipe]

What is the length of the pipe being measured?
reference_items.figure_description: A horizontal ruler labeled "Meters (m)" at the top has major tick marks from 0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.1, with minor tick marks halfway between each major tick mark (representing increments of 0.05). Below the ruler, a gray cylindrical pipe is positioned horizontally. Dimension lines with arrows indicate the length being measured from the left end of the pipe, which aligns with 0 on the ruler, to the right end of the pipe, which aligns with the tick mark halfway between 0.8 and 0.9.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
